Shares M-01's root cause (L416 re-anchor) and the identical 63.4% figure, zero attacker payoff; independent impact is the dust tail-stall (~300 wei). Folded into M-01 as the access-control/tail-stall angle. Reconciled by fingerprint/root-cause (ledger entry M-02), not by label.

classificationReport.codeVerification: Severities grounded by reading src/Phlimbo.sol: _updatePool L389-426 (rate re-anchor L416 + accStablePerShare floor L410, rewardBalance debit L413), _claimRewards L432-455 (debt-underflow path L440/L446), pauseWithdraw L245-261 (no _updatePhUSDEmissionRate, no debt rebase, no dust guard), emergencyTransfer L214-227 (full drain + unconditional _pause), setPauser L206-208, unpause L197-199 (pauser-gated -> pauser==0 = permanent pause).

classifiedFindings.label: M-01
classifiedFindings.title: "Linear Depletion" implemented as exponential decay: rewardPerSecond re-anchored on every interaction (~63% delivered in-window, stranded tail)

classification.assetImpact: Reward stream under-delivered: each tranche pays only ~1-(1-1/e) ~ 63% within its intended depletion window; the ~37% remainder is pushed out into an ever-receding tail and a residual is stranded in rewardBalance. No principal at risk; no theft. Affects every staker passively. Stranded remainder is recoverable only by owner emergencyTransfer.
attackPath: 1. No attacker required - emergent from normal usage.
2. collectReward sets rewardPerSecond = rewardBalance*PRECISION/depletionDuration (L283).
3. On every stake/withdraw/claim/collectReward, _updatePool distributes, debits rewardBalance, then RE-ANCHORS rewardPerSecond = (reduced rewardBalance)*PRECISION/depletionDuration (L416).
4. Re-anchoring restarts the full depletion window against a shrunk balance on each interaction, converting linear depletion into exponential decay.
5. Over one nominal window only ~63% is delivered; the tail stalls when per-update reward < 1 wei/share.
classification.likelihood: high - occurs on ordinary protocol activity; the more interactions, the worse the under-delivery (decreasing in N).
classification.assumptions: Standard staking activity; rewardBalance>0; totalStaked>0. Quantified Tier-3 CONFIRMED.

classifiedFindings.justification: Capped at Medium: this is in-motion (still-streaming) reward yield, not matured yield or principal, and the under-delivered remainder is owner-recoverable - so per the Loss-of-Yield rule it cannot exceed Medium. It clears Medium because the protocol's headline advertised function (Linear Depletion) is materially degraded and value (reward delivery) leaks/strands with stated assumptions. BORDERLINE Medium-vs-Low: argues toward Low because nothing is permanently lost (owner can sweep the tail) and no party is enriched; argues toward Medium because under-delivery is large (~37% in-window), systemic, and affects every staker on every cycle. Held at Medium. Design-decision tension (designDecisions[2] describes the recompute mechanism, but CLAUDE.md labels it 'the V1 rate-recompute BUG' and PhlimboV2/story-020 removes it) is disclosed in the finding; the described mechanism does not bless the emergent impact, so it is reported, not suppressed.
classifiedFindings.borderlineFlag: BORDERLINE Medium-vs-Low (no permanent loss / no enrichment vs large systemic under-delivery). Also carries a spec-faithfulness dimension (advertised 'Linear Depletion' vs delivered exponential) but is routed as an HM value-leak at honest severity per Law 1; the dedicated faithfulness lens for the pauseWithdraw story is F-01/DEDUP-008.

classifiedFindings.label: L-06
classifiedFindings.reclassNote: Downgraded from Medium per severity-auditor (phlimbo-ea-04): self-inflicted (msg.sender-only pauseWithdraw), multi-gated, principal recoverable via re-pause; permanent-strand corner captured by C-01. User-approved.
classifiedFindings.title: Partial pauseWithdraw leaves reward debt anchored to pre-withdraw amount -> next claim/withdraw/stake underflow-reverts (account brick)

classification.assetImpact: Availability/function impact on the affected account: phUSD+stable rewards become permanently unclaimable and the remaining staked principal is locked against the normal exit paths. Remaining principal is recoverable ONLY while the contract is paused, via a further pauseWithdraw (which needs a live, valid pauser). No theft.
attackPath: 1. Contract is paused; user calls pauseWithdraw(partial) (L245). user.amount and totalStaked decrease (L251/254) but phUSDDebt/stableDebt are NOT rebased.
2. Debt is now anchored to the larger pre-withdraw amount.
3. After unpause, any claim/withdraw/stake calls _claimRewards, computing (smaller user.amount * accPerShare)/PRECISION - (larger debt) -> Panic 0x11 underflow (L440/L446).
4. All normal paths revert; the remaining principal is locked unless the contract is paused again and the user does a full pauseWithdraw.
classification.likelihood: medium - requires a paused state and a PARTIAL pauseWithdraw, a plausible legitimate emergency action; the bricking consequence is non-obvious to the user.
classification.assumptions: User performs a partial (not full) pauseWithdraw while paused and does not fully exit before unpause.
classification.externalRequirements: Contract must be paused for the trigger AND for the only recovery path (needs a valid pauser); after unpause with no re-pause, remaining principal is stuck.

classifiedFindings.justification: Medium per C4: assets not directly stolen, but account-level availability is broken and the remaining principal becomes a conditional lock recoverable only via an external requirement (re-pause by a valid pauser). Not High: no attacker profit, no protocol-wide theft, and principal is recoverable while paused. BORDERLINE Medium-vs-Low: self-inflicted (msg.sender-only) and only reachable during pause pull toward Low; but partial emergency exit is a realistic action and the brick is a non-obvious code defect (missing debt rebase), and the lock-after-unpause can permanently strand principal if no re-pause occurs - which pulls firmly to Medium. Held at Medium (matches prior ledger M-01). NOT suppressed under KI-4: the blessed forfeiture note covers only 'does not claim/update pool', not this downstream stale-debt brick.
classifiedFindings.borderlineFlag: BORDERLINE Medium-vs-Low: self-inflicted + pause-gated trigger vs non-obvious defect + post-unpause principal lock. Held Medium.

classifiedFindings.label: L-01
classifiedFindings.title: CEI violation in stake/withdraw/claim (debt settled after phUSD.mint / rewardToken.transfer, no nonReentrant) -> conditional re-entry N-claim

classification.assetImpact: Defense-in-depth gap only under current scope. IF a callback-capable reward/phUSD token (ERC777/hooked) were wired, an attacker could re-enter claim before debt is rebased and drain reward/over-mint phUSD (conditional High). Under the in-scope standard-ERC20 phUSD (no mint callback) + standard stablecoin reward, it is NOT triggerable.
attackPath: 1. (Conditional) reward or phUSD token has a transfer/mint hook.

2. _claimRewards mints phUSD (L442) / transfers reward (L448) BEFORE the caller rebases phUSDDebt/stableDebt (debt set after _claimRewards returns in claim/stake/withdraw); stake/withdraw/claim lack nonReentrant.
3. Hook re-enters claim() with stale debt -> repeated payout.
4. Not reachable today: phUSD.mint has no callback and the stable reward is a standard ERC20.
classification.likelihood: low - requires a non-standard callback token, which is outside the in-scope token set and on the known-invalid list.
classification.assumptions: Realistic path assumes only the deployed standard tokens.
classification.externalRequirements: A hooked/ERC777 token wired onto the reward or phUSD path (not the case today).

classifiedFindings.justification: Realistic severity Low: the CEI ordering defect is real and worth fixing as defense-in-depth (add nonReentrant / settle debt before external calls), but the only path to asset loss requires a callback-capable token, which the repo's known-invalid policy excludes from in-scope tokens. No demonstrated trigger on the deployed token set. Classified Low (matches ledger L-09); the conditional-High is documented but not assigned because it rests on an out-of-scope token assumption (Rule 4: conservative when uncertain).
classifiedFindings.borderlineFlag: Conditional: escalates to High ONLY if a hook/callback token is introduced onto the reward/phUSD path; under in-scope tokens it is Low.

classifiedFindings.label: L-07
classifiedFindings.reclassNote: Downgraded from Medium per severity-auditor (phlimbo-ea-04): shares M-01's root cause (L416 re-anchor) and identical 63.4% figure, zero attacker payoff, independent impact is dust tail-stall (~300 wei); folded into M-01 as the access-control/tail-stall angle. User-approved.
classifiedFindings.title: Permissionless collectReward (+ free non-staker claim() poke) re-anchors rewardPerSecond at gas-only cost, forcing worst-case decay / tail stall

classification.assetImpact: Availability / value-delivery degradation of the reward stream. An attacker repeatedly forces _updatePool re-anchoring, driving DEDUP-001's exponential decay to its worst case and stalling the tail (remaining rewardBalance never distributes once per-update reward floors to 0). Stalled tail recoverable only by owner emergencyTransfer. Attacker profit is ZERO (pure value-denial); cost is gas only.
attackPath: 1. Attacker calls claim() as a NON-staker: _claimRewards returns early (amount==0) but _updatePool still runs and re-anchors rewardPerSecond (L416). No tokens or approval needed.
2. (Or) attacker calls collectReward(1 wei) - permissionless (L270) - to the same effect plus a forced rate recompute (L283).
3. Repeat each block to maximize re-anchoring frequency, pushing delivery toward the decreasing-in-N worst case delivered = 1-(1-T/(N*D))^N.
4. Below the ~D/12 reward-wei threshold the per-update distribution floors to 0 and the tail permanently stalls.
classification.likelihood: medium - trivially callable by anyone at gas-only cost, but yields the attacker nothing, so only a griefer with no profit motive would do it; the same decay also occurs organically.
classification.assumptions: Active reward stream; griefer willing to pay gas for pure denial.

classifiedFindings.justification: Medium per C4: protocol function/availability (reward delivery) is impaired and value (the stranded/stalled tail) leaks, with the stated assumption of a gas-paying griefer. Not High: zero asset theft, attacker gains nothing, principal untouched, tail owner-recoverable. BORDERLINE Medium-vs-Low: pure zero-payoff griefing and large overlap with DEDUP-001's organic decay argue Low; the permissionless, free, repeatable amplification to a permanent tail-stall (a concrete availability harm) argues Medium. Held at Medium (matches ledger M-02), enriched this run with the non-staker claim() poke vector and the D/12 tail-stall threshold.
classifiedFindings.borderlineFlag: BORDERLINE Medium-vs-Low: zero-payoff griefing / overlaps DEDUP-001 vs free permissionless amplification to permanent tail-stall. Held Medium.

classifiedFindings.label: M-04
classifiedFindings.title: pause -> pauseWithdraw -> unpause OVER-MINTS phUSD: stale phUSDPerSecond (sized for pre-pause totalStaked) accrues over the shrunken stake on unpause

classification.assetImpact: Uncapped phUSD supply inflation: remaining stakers are minted phUSD at an over-rate of S0/S1 (pre-pause / post-pauseWithdraw totalStaked) for the entire window between unpause and the next stake/withdraw that recomputes the rate. The over-minted phUSD is value created from nothing, diluting all phUSD holders and breaking the APY invariant (story-006 / INV-7). No principal theft.
attackPath: 1. desiredAPYBps > 0, so phUSDPerSecond is non-zero (set on last stake/withdraw from pre-pause totalStaked = S0).
2. Contract is paused; one or more users pauseWithdraw, dropping totalStaked to S1 < S0. pauseWithdraw does NOT call _updatePhUSDEmissionRate (L245-261), so phUSDPerSecond stays sized for S0.
3. Contract is unpaused. _updatePool accrues phUSDReward = timeElapsed * phUSDPerSecond and divides by the smaller S1 (L420-422) -> accPhUSDPerShare inflated by factor S0/S1.
4. claim() does NOT recompute the emission rate, so the stale over-rate persists until the next stake/withdraw; remaining stakers claim S0/S1 x intended phUSD.
classification.likelihood: medium-low - requires a full pause + partial pauseWithdraw + unpause cycle AND a non-zero APY; the LIVE deployment is documented zero-APY (KI-10), which fully immunizes the phUSD stream.
classification.assumptions: Operator has enabled a non-zero desiredAPYBps; at least one user exits via pauseWithdraw during the pause; a non-trivial window elapses before the next stake/withdraw.
classification.externalRequirements: Non-zero APY mode (operator-selectable, NOT the current live config) + pauser-driven pause/unpause around a pauseWithdraw.

classifiedFindings.justification: Medium per C4: a value leak (phUSD inflation to remaining stakers) with clearly stated assumptions and external requirements (non-zero APY + pause/pauseWithdraw/unpause sequence). Not suppressed under KI-4 (forfeiture does not cover over-minting to OTHER stakers) or KI-10 (zero-APY only lowers likelihood). BORDERLINE Medium-vs-High-if-APY>0: under a non-zero APY deployment with a long inter-interaction window and large S0/S1, the inflation is uncapped and could rise to High (direct unbounded value creation) - re-evaluate as High if such a config ships. Held at Medium because the live zero-APY config immunizes it, the over-mint window is bounded by the next stake/withdraw, and the trigger needs an operator-selected mode plus a pause sequence. Tagged a Law-3 footgun: a non-malicious operator enabling APY would be surprised that a pauseWithdraw during pause inflates phUSD on unpause; safe-config guidance = recompute the emission rate inside pauseWithdraw (or on unpause).
classifiedFindings.borderlineFlag: BORDERLINE Medium-vs-High-if-APY>0: live zero-APY -> Medium; a shipped non-zero-APY config with a long stale window -> re-classify as High (uncapped inflation).

classifiedFindings.label: C-01
classifiedFindings.title: setPauser(0) + emergencyTransfer permanently bricks ALL withdrawals (force-paused, no valid unpauser, pauseWithdraw escape drained, accounting never zeroed) - owner footgun

classification.assetImpact: Operational hazard: the contract becomes permanently paused with non-zeroed accounting and a dead escape hatch. The funds themselves are removed by the (owner-trusted) emergencyTransfer drain, so the footgun's MARGINAL impact is the irreversible paused/locked state, not additional asset loss beyond the trusted sweep.
attackPath: 1. Owner calls setPauser(0) - documented as 'disable pausing' (L204), sounds benign (L206-208).
2. A later emergency prompts emergencyTransfer: it sweeps all phUSD + reward (L218-223) and unconditionally _pause()s (L226).
3. unpause() requires msg.sender == pauser (L197-198); with pauser==0 no account can ever unpause -> permanent pause.

4. pauseWithdraw still passes whenPaused but its safeTransfer reverts (balance already drained), and user.amount/totalStaked were never zeroed -> escape hatch is dead and accounting is permanently inconsistent.
classification.likelihood: low - requires the specific (documented) setPauser(0) choice to coincide with an emergencyTransfer; non-obvious composition.
classification.assumptions: Non-malicious owner who chose setPauser(0) and then needs emergencyTransfer.
classification.externalRequirements: Owner has set pauser to address(0) prior to (or without later restoring before) the drain.

classifiedFindings.justification: Classified Centralization (operational hazard), not High and not a malicious-owner finding. The drain itself is an obvious, trusted owner power (KI-5 / designDecisions[4]) and is suppressed as such. What is KEPT is the NON-OBVIOUS Law-3 footgun: a competent non-malicious owner would be surprised that the documented 'disable pausing' (setPauser(0)) turns emergencyTransfer's auto-pause into an irreversible lock and silently leaves accounting non-zeroed. Severity stays at Centralization rather than escalating to High under the footgun rule because the asset loss is the trusted drain, not the footgun - the footgun adds only the permanent-paused/dead-escape-hatch state on funds that are already (trustedly) gone. Safe-config guidance: do not run with pauser==address(0) while emergencyTransfer is usable; zero user/total accounting (or skip the auto-pause) in emergencyTransfer.
classifiedFindings.borderlineFlag: Footgun, not malicious-admin. Marginal harm = permanent-pause state on already-drained funds, so capped at Centralization (would rise to High only if the footgun itself caused asset loss beyond the trusted drain - it does not).

classifiedFindings.label: L-02
classifiedFindings.title: pauseWithdraw bypasses the MINIMUM_STAKE / dust-forces-full-exit rule (INV-6 weakening); sub-minimum positions + dusted totalStaked (emission can floor to 0)

classification.assetImpact: State-handling / invariant weakening. pauseWithdraw omits the dust guard that withdraw() enforces (L346-351), so users can leave sub-MINIMUM_STAKE positions and dust totalStaked, making the low-stake/low-APY dust regime (where phUSD emission floors to 0, cf. L-13) reachable. No theft; the catastrophic accumulator-overflow facet was REFUTED by symbolic analysis (out of realistic range).
attackPath: 1. Contract paused; user pauseWithdraw(amount) leaving 0 < remaining < MINIMUM_STAKE (no dust guard at L245-261).
2. totalStaked can be driven to dust while positions persist.

3. In the dust regime, _updatePhUSDEmissionRate / per-share math can floor emission to 0 (under-emission), weakening the first-depositor/precision mitigation INV-6 enforced elsewhere by MINIMUM_STAKE.
classification.likelihood: low - reachable only during pause; impact is degraded precision/under-emission, not loss.
classification.assumptions: Paused state; user opts to leave a dust position.

classifiedFindings.justification: Low per C4: this is incorrect state handling / a deviation from the MINIMUM_STAKE invariant (INV-6) that withdraw() upholds but pauseWithdraw skips. The reachable consequence (dust-regime emission flooring to 0) is itself a low-severity precision/under-emission effect, and the severe overflow facet was refuted. Not suppressed under KI-2 (which blesses MINIMUM_STAKE as a mitigation, not pauseWithdraw bypassing it) or KI-3 (the dust handler lives on withdraw(); pauseWithdraw's absence of it is the gap). Distinct root cause from L-13 (which it only shares a consequence with). Classified Low.
classifiedFindings.borderlineFlag: None significant - clean Low (invariant weakening; overflow facet refuted, dust-emission consequence is low-impact).

classifiedFindings.label: F-01
classifiedFindings.title: FAITHFULNESS: emergencyTransfer breaks story-008 HIGH-5's promise of a safe pauseWithdraw exit after a drain - post-drain pauseWithdraw reverts for everyone

classification.assetImpact: No direct protocol value loss in the intended flow: the emergencyTransfer drain is owner-trusted and redistribution is intended off-chain (story-049). The deviation is that story-008 HIGH-5 advertises an on-chain guarantee that users can 'safely exit via pauseWithdraw' after an emergency - which does NOT hold, because post-drain the contract is paused with zero balance, so pauseWithdraw reverts for everyone.
attackPath: 1. Story-008 HIGH-5 states users retain a safe pauseWithdraw exit after emergency action.
2. emergencyTransfer drains all balances and _pause()s (L214-227).
3. Any post-drain pauseWithdraw (L257 safeTransfer) reverts for lack of balance -> the advertised on-chain recovery promise is unmet.
classification.likelihood: n/a (spec-conformance deviation, surfaced regardless of exploit likelihood per Law 2).

classifiedFindings.justification: Routed to the spec-conformance report as F-01 with faithfulness=true (Law 2): a behavioural deviation from story-008 HIGH-5's stated on-chain recovery guarantee. The drain is owner-trusted (suppressed framing), and the intended redistribution is off-chain (story-049), so there is no direct value loss in the faithful flow - hence honest severity Low. It is the Law-2 lens on the same mechanism whose security manifestation is C-01/DEDUP-006; kept distinct (faithfulness rootCauseClass) and visible to the owner rather than buried in QA/gas noise.
classifiedFindings.borderlineFlag: Faithfulness finding: F-label + Low severity. No direct value loss in the intended off-chain-redistribution flow; the security manifestation is carried by C-01.

classifiedFindings.label: L-03
classifiedFindings.title: Stable reward stranding via per-share rounding: rewardBalance debited in full while accStablePerShare floors -> floored remainder permanently uncredited

classification.assetImpact: Dust-level stable reward stranding. Each update debits rewardBalance by toDistribute in full (L413) but credits accStablePerShare with floor(toDistribute*PRECISION/totalStaked) (L410); the floored remainder is never credited to any share and becomes permanently uncreditable - though owner-recoverable via emergencyTransfer. Bounded < totalStaked/PRECISION (+1 wei) per update; no over-distribution (INV-4 preserved/proved).
attackPath: 1. No attacker - emergent rounding loss.
2. Per update, the integer floor at L410 drops a sub-share remainder while L413 still removes the full toDistribute from rewardBalance.
3. Frequent small updates (amplified by DEDUP-001/DEDUP-004) accumulate many small strands.
classification.likelihood: high frequency but dust magnitude per occurrence.
classification.externalRequirements: None; owner can sweep stranded dust.

classifiedFindings.justification: Low per the Loss-of-Fees/rounding rule: integer-floor remainder stranding is dust-magnitude per update (bounded < totalStaked/PRECISION), causes no over-distribution (proved), and is owner-recoverable. Not any documented KI or design decision. Independent defect with an independent fix (carry the remainder forward). Tier-3 CONFIRMED (strand>0 counterexample; bound + no-overcredit proved). Classified Low.
classifiedFindings.borderlineFlag: None - dust rounding -> clean Low/QA-tier (kept as Low; bounded, no over-distribution, owner-recoverable).

classifiedFindings.label: L-04
classifiedFindings.title: setPauser does not emit an event on rotation of the security-critical pauser role (observability gap)

classification.assetImpact: None - observability/monitoring gap only. Rotating the security-critical pauser role (L206-208) emits no event, hindering off-chain monitoring and incident response.
attackPath: 1. Owner calls setPauser(newPauser); no event is emitted.
2. Off-chain monitors cannot detect the role change without polling storage.

classifiedFindings.justification: QA/Low per repo policy (missing-event is QA at best). No state corruption or value impact - purely an observability shortfall on a sensitive role. The companion missing-zero-check on setPauser was correctly NOT raised because setPauser(0) is documented-intentional ('disable pausing'). Classified Low/QA (matches ledger L-04).

classifiedFindings.label: L-05
classifiedFindings.title: pendingPhUSD / pendingStable views revert (Panic 0x11) for a post-pauseWithdraw user instead of returning 0 (off-chain integration DoS)

classification.assetImpact: Off-chain integration availability only. After a partial pauseWithdraw leaves stale debt, pendingPhUSD/pendingStable compute (smaller amount * accPerShare)/PRECISION - (larger debt) and revert with Panic 0x11 (L489 and the pendingStable analogue) instead of returning 0, breaking dashboards/integrators that read these views. No on-chain asset impact.
attackPath: 1. User does a partial pauseWithdraw (stale debt, as in DEDUP-002).
2. Any caller of pendingPhUSD(user)/pendingStable(user) hits the underflow and the view reverts.
3. Off-chain consumers expecting a uint256 get a revert -> integration DoS.
classification.likelihood: low-medium - same precondition as DEDUP-002; affects read-only integrators.
classification.assumptions: A user has stale debt from a prior partial pauseWithdraw.
classification.externalRequirements: Off-chain consumers relying on these view functions.

classifiedFindings.justification: Low/QA per the View-Functions rule (view-function issues are Low/QA at best). It shares the on-chain root cause with M-02/DEDUP-002 but is kept separate: this is a read-side off-chain DoS with a clamp-view fix, versus M-02's on-chain account brick with a debt-rebase fix. No funds at risk from the view itself. Classified Low/QA (matches ledger L-14).
classifiedFindings.borderlineFlag: None - view-function revert -> Low/QA (the underlying on-chain brick is carried by M-02).
